evals.name: governed-cf-and-kyma-topology
evals.description: The account workflow uses governed account setup and collects optional environment details.

files.content:
# Scenario

Create dev and prod subaccounts for the billing application.

# BTP Governance

## Regions
- Allowed: eu10
- Forbidden: none
- Data residency: EU only
- Compliance reason: GDPR
- Preferred region: eu10

## Account Setup
- Global account subdomain: acme-global
- Allowed environments: Cloud Foundry, Kyma

## Naming
- Subaccount pattern: acme-{env}-billing
- Pattern tokens: {env} = environment tier, {space} = space purpose
- Cloud Foundry org pattern: acme-{env}-billing
- Kyma environment pattern: acme-{env}-billing-kyma
- Cloud Foundry space pattern: acme-{env}-{space}
- Environments: dev, prod
- Directory structure: flat
- Max name length: 60

turns.content: Define the account topology for this project.
For dev create both environments: the CF org is acme-dev-billing with spaces acme-dev-dev and acme-dev-qa; the Kyma environment is acme-dev-billing-kyma. For prod create no runtime environment.
Accept the usage and beta settings.

assertions.text: Uses acme-global as the global account subdomain without asking for a GUID or another global account identifier
Collects that dev has both Cloud Foundry and Kyma and that prod has no runtime environment
Collects and validates the two named Cloud Foundry spaces only after Cloud Foundry is selected

Shows a confirmation table before writing, then writes specs/landscape.md containing the governed global account subdomain, selected environment and space details, and inferred dev/prod usage and beta_enabled values

# Scenario

Create dev and prod subaccounts for the billing application.

# BTP Governance

## Regions
- Allowed: eu10
- Forbidden: none

## Account Setup
- Global account subdomain: acme-global
- Allowed environments: Cloud Foundry

## Naming
- Subaccount pattern: acme-{env}-billing
- Pattern tokens: {env} = environment tier
- Cloud Foundry org pattern: acme-{env}-billing
- Kyma environment pattern: acme-{env}-billing-kyma
- Cloud Foundry space pattern: acme-{env}-{space}
- Environments: dev, prod
- Directory structure: hierarchical
- Max name length: 60

turns.content: Define the account topology for this project.
Use one managed directory per tier (acme-dev-dir, acme-prod-dir), each with ENTITLEMENTS only. Assign each subaccount to its tier directory. No shared subaccounts. No runtime environments.
Accept the usage and beta settings.

assertions.text: Because governance has no Directory management/assignment/shared fields, it discusses managed vs. unmanaged directories (with features and trade-offs), assignment, and shared subaccounts rather than inventing them
Writes a ## Directories section with acme-dev-dir and acme-prod-dir as managed whose features include DEFAULT and ENTITLEMENTS and with no subdomain
Records each subaccount's Directory assignment and Shared: false in specs/landscape.md

# Scenario

Create a shared connectivity subaccount plus a dev subaccount.

# BTP Governance

## Regions
- Allowed: eu10
- Forbidden: none

## Account Setup
- Global account subdomain: acme-global
- Allowed environments: Cloud Foundry
- Directory management: managed
- Directory features: ENTITLEMENTS, AUTHORIZATIONS
- Subaccount directory assignment: one directory per environment tier
- Shared subaccounts: acme-shared-connectivity -> platform team

## Naming
- Subaccount pattern: acme-{env}-{app}
- Pattern tokens: {env} = environment tier, {app} = application identifier
- Cloud Foundry org pattern: acme-{env}-{app}
- Kyma environment pattern: acme-{env}-{app}-kyma
- Cloud Foundry space pattern: acme-{env}-{space}
- Environments: shared, dev
- Directory structure: hierarchical
- Max name length: 60

turns.content: Define the account topology for this project.
Create acme-shared-connectivity and acme-dev-billing, both with no runtime environment.
Accept the usage and beta settings.

assertions.text: Applies the governed directory policy without re-asking the managed/unmanaged, feature-set, assignment, or shared questions

Records the concrete non-governed facts in specs/landscape.md — directory names and, because the governed feature set includes AUTHORIZATIONS, a directory subdomain — without restating the governed managed posture or feature set
Does not duplicate the governed Shared subaccounts entry in specs/landscape.md; acme-shared-connectivity's shared designation stays in memory/governance.md
